name: Gates of Orgrimmar
summary: At Orgrimmar's southern gate, timber and iron guard the opening cut into northern Durotar's red rock. Through it, the arid wastes give way to the Valley of Strength, the capital's busy commons. The gate proclaims the Horde's endurance and strength in war.

sections.title: The Bastion of Durotar
sections.body: Orgrimmar's main gate guards the great chasm cut into the mountains around the city. Wooden palisades rise above the entrance, braced with iron spikes and watchtowers. Travelers from Razor Hill and Durotar's scrublands find a grand welcome—and a warning to anyone who threatens the new Horde. Armed Orgrimmar Grunts patrol the approach and watch all who enter.

sections.title: Threshold to the Valley
sections.body: Beyond the gate's shadowed arch, you enter the Valley of Strength, Orgrimmar's civic and martial heart. The tunnel narrows the way for envoys, merchants, and warriors, while sentries watch those who pass. Here, Warchief Thrall's dream takes shape: a secure refuge carved from the harsh desert, where the Horde's many peoples can walk together without fear.

faq.q: Where do the Gates of Orgrimmar lead?
faq.answer: The Gates of Orgrimmar lead from northern Durotar into the Valley of Strength, the city's main entrance and central commons.
Orgrimmar Grunts guard the front gates and watch for hostile infiltrators and wild beasts.

faq.q: Why is the entrance fortified with wood and spikes?
faq.answer: Wooden palisades and iron spikes follow orcish frontier defenses. Sturdy timber from nearby lands makes a formidable choke point in the canyon walls.

faq.q: Can Alliance players pass through this gate?
faq.answer: Alliance members who try to pass through the main gate face hostile veteran guards, ready to strike down Horde enemies on sight.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you can see the gates as a place of safety and belonging, a hard-won homeland forged under Warchief Thrall's leadership.
As an Alliance scout or infiltrator, you face one of Kalimdor's most heavily guarded bottlenecks, nearly impossible to breach by frontal assault.
